dwigraha.note: Two grahas occupying one sign, and what the verse says of the native. Read from N. Chidambaram Iyer's 1885 translation; Mantreswara gives the same twenty-one readings at Phaladeepika ch. 18 vv. 1 to 5. Phaladeepika ch. 18 v. 5 says in the verse that more than two grahas in a house are read by combining the readings of every pair they contain, which is what one rule a pair does of itself; Brihat Jataka ch. 14 v. 5 says only that “in the case of other planetary yogas the effects described shall be determined and applied”, and it is Iyer's note (a) on that verse, not Varahamihira, that spells the pairwise split out.

inRasi.note: A graha in a sign, and what the chapter says of the native. Read from R. Santhanam's translation of Kalyana Varma's Saravali, one chapter to a graha, the signs in order from Aries. The readings that follow in each chapter, of the same graha under each other graha's aspect, are the aspectedInRasi family. Ch. 23 v. 88 says a sign's reading comes in full where the sign, its lord and the graha are strong, to be judged by exaltation and debilitation: it weighs a reading and bars none, so it is no condition here.

aspectedInRasi.note: A graha in a sign under another graha's aspect, and what the chapter says of the native. Read from the 1907 Nirnaya Sagar print of Kalyana Varma's Saravali (ed. V. Subrahmanya Sastri), chs. 22 to 29, the verses after each graha's twelve signs; the verse numbers are that print's. A chapter reads the two signs of one lord in a verse, and the Moon's chapter each sign alone, so one verse stands for a rule in each sign it covers. The Sun, Mercury and Venus never stand far enough apart for one to aspect another, so the verses the chapters print for those pairs are not rules: 42 verses, two in each of the seven groups of the Sun's, Mercury's and Venus's chapters. Ch. 23 v. 86 (Santhanam's v. 88) says a sign's reading comes in full where the sign, its lord and the graha are strong: it weighs a reading and bars none, so it is no condition here. Ch. 24 vv. 22 to 23 weigh the Moon's aspect readings by her navamsa, full in vargottama, middling in her own, small in another's, and set them aside where the navamsa's lord is strong, naming no measure of strength; that is recorded and not encoded, so each reading is what its verse says wherever the aspect holds.

risingPart.note: The sign that rises, and the part of it, and what the chapter says of the native. Read from R. Santhanam's translation of Kalyana Varma's Saravali, the signs in order from Aries and the parts in order from the beginning of each sign; the Sanskrit prints number the chapters on the parts one lower, the horas ch. 48, and their verses alike. Each chapter says when its effects come in full, and none says what follows otherwise, so none is built: ch. 48 where the rising sign or its lord is strong; ch. 49 v. 25 where a luminary is strong and aspected by the lord of the hora (the lagna's lord, as the translations read it) or that lord is in a kendra; ch. 50 v. 37 where the decanate's sign is strong or aspected by its lord ("and" in the Hindi commentary); ch. 51 v. 1 by the stronger of the navamsa lagna's lord and the Moon's navamsa dispositor. The second decanates of Gemini and of Cancer are printed with one reading between them in the translation read, and both ship as printed.

carried.name: DWADASAMSA
carried.note: The lagna in a dwadasamsa of its sign: ch. 51 v. 110 says what was said of each rising sign is to be said of the dwadasamsa too, and the dwadasamsas count from the sign itself (ch. 3 v. 13), so the n-th of a sign reads as ch. 48's lagna in the sign n − 1 on. Read in R. Santhanam's translation and Chaturvedi's 1967 edition (rāśiphalaṃ); the 1907 Nirnaya Sagar print reads aṃśādiphalaṃ, the navamsa's, which gives no rule from nine readings to twelve parts. The verse's second half reads the remaining divisions as the saptamsa is read, and Saravali gives no saptamsa reading, so nothing is built of it.

pairInAngle.note: Two grahas sharing an angle, and what the chapter says of the native. Read from R. Santhanam's translation of Kalyana Varma's Saravali, the pairs in the chapter's own order — the Sun first — and within a pair the ascendant, the fourth, the seventh and the tenth. This is the only family in the texts read that keys a reading to a set of grahas in a *named* house; v. 87 closes the chapter by declining to write the same for three, four, five or six grahas in an angle, so nothing of that shape ships. Verse 46 adds that the Moon with benefics is always beneficial and the Moon with Mars or Saturn always inauspicious except in the tenth, which is what these readings of hers already say.

saravaliTogether.note: Grahas of the seven sharing one sign, and what the chapter says of the native: chs. 15 to 19 read every pair, three, four, five and six of them in turn. Read in the 1907 Nirnaya Sagar print of Kalyana Varma's Saravali, each verse naming its grahas; the readings are paraphrased. A set fires whenever its grahas share a sign, as Jataka Parijata's lists do, so a sign holding three grahas also answers its three pairs. Ch. 18 prints twenty-two verses for its twenty-one sets, v. 13 naming the five v. 20 names; v. 20 stands at that set's place in the run and is the one built (C479).
